info.title: Agent Switchboard Directory API
info.summary: Read-only catalog of AI agents, MCP servers, and agentic developer tools.
info.description: Agent Switchboard is a public discovery directory. Use this API to answer questions like 'is there an agent that does X?' or 'which listed products expose an MCP server?'. There is no authentication, no user account, and no write access. The /api/ endpoints allow 120 requests per minute per IP and answer 429 with Retry-After past that; cached responses do not count, and /api/mcp has its own limits. This API does not proxy the underlying products — it only returns Switchboard listings. For interactive tool-shaped access, an MCP server is also available at /api/mcp. Listing data returned by this API is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (attribution required; commercial reuse needs a license: https://agentswitchboard.dev/contact). The API definition itself is MIT.

get.description: Relevance-ranked search over name, description, skills, categories, tags, and provider. Empty `q` lists published agents in catalog order: featured first, then A→Z. With `q`, results are ranked by relevance and equal scores keep that featured-first order. `sort` can order them by newest, most skills, or name instead. Filter by task, category slug, access methods, `official`, `verified`, `auth`, and/or `since` (when a listing was added). With a `task` and no `q`, results are best fit first. Paginate with `total` + `offset` + `limit`, `page`, or by following `next`. A page holds at most 50 listings; for bulk work, read the /agents.json index and the /catalog pages it links.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text query. Empty string or omitted = no text filter.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Task slug from GET /api/tasks, e.g. `query-a-database`: keeps only the listings that do that job, best fit first. Case-insensitive. An unknown slug returns 400 with `error: "unknown_task"`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category slug from GET /api/categories, e.g. `code-devtools`.

parameters.name: access
parameters.description: One or more of `api`, `mcp`, `cli`, `browser-extension`. `extension` is accepted as an alias of `browser-extension`. Case-insensitive. Comma-separate to require all (`access=api,mcp`). Unknown values are ignored.

parameters.name: official
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`, `yes`) returns only first-party listings from major vendors; any other value applies no filter. Combines with `category`, `access`, and `q`.

parameters.name: verified
parameters.description: `true` (or `1`, `yes`) returns only Verified listings: checked to work, re-checked monthly. Any other value applies no filter.

parameters.name: auth
parameters.description: Only listings with this auth type: `none` (no key or sign-in needed), `apiKey`, `oauth2`, or `bearer`. Case-insensitive. A listing has one auth type, so comma-separated values mean any of them (`auth=none,apiKey`). Unknown values are ignored.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only listings added to the directory on or after this day (UTC): a date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (a full timestamp counts by its day), or a number of days back with today included (`since=7` is the last 7 days, `since=1` today), from 1 to 3650. The response echoes the first day kept as `since`. Anything else returns 400 with `error: "invalid_since"`. Add `sort=newest` to list the newest first.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Result order. `relevance` (default): with `q`, best match first; without, best fit first for a `task`, else featured first, then A→Z. `newest`: most recently added first. `skills`: most skills first. `name`: A→Z. Ties keep the default order. Unknown values mean `relevance`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `organic`: ignore featured placement, so the default order and ties are A→Z. WebMCP uses it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Clamped to 1–50. Default 10.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of matches to skip. Default 0. Wins over `page` when both are sent.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number from 1, in steps of `limit`: `page=3&limit=20` is `offset=40`. Ignored when `offset` is sent. Default 1.

agents.name: AgentMail
agents.description: Email inbox API built for AI agents.

400.description: `task` is not a task slug from GET /api/tasks (`error: "unknown_task"`), or `since` is neither a date nor a number of days (`error: "invalid_since"`).

get.description: Full listing for a published agent: the searchAgents fields (including `verified`, `official`, `featured` and `sponsored`) plus skills, auth type, provider homepage, tags, streaming and push flags. Use a `slug` returned by searchAgents. Unpublished or unknown slugs return 404.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Stable listing identifier, e.g. `agentmail`.

404.description: No published agent with that slug.

get.summary: Listings that could stand in for one
get.description: The listings that could stand in for one, strongest match first, as its page /agents/{slug}/alternatives lists them. Each is in the listing's main category, offers at least one of its access methods, and overlaps on what it does (shared skills and tags, rarer ones counting for more), and says why. Up to 8; fewer, or none, rather than a weak match. A listing gets an alternatives page (`url`) only with at least 3. Unknown or no-longer-listed slugs return 404.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Stable listing identifier, e.g. `deepgram`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most alternatives to return. Clamped to 1–8. Default 8.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `organic`: break score ties A→Z instead of featured first. WebMCP uses it.

404.description: No published agent with that slug.

get.description: Every category with a live count of published agents. Use `slug` as the `category` query parameter on searchAgents.

Stacks are editor-picked sets of listings that together do one job, each listing with why it is in the stack. In the order /stacks shows them: the stack of the week first. `stackOfTheWeek` is the slug of the newest stack tied to a weekly drop.

200.description: Every stack, the stack of the week first.

get.description: One stack with its listings in order, each with why it is in the stack. Use a `slug` returned by listStacks. Unknown slugs return 404.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Stable stack identifier, e.g. `research-analyst`.

get.description: Tasks are jobs ("query a database", "transcribe audio"), each with how many listings do it. Use a task's `slug` as the `task` parameter on searchAgents to filter and page those listings, best fit first, or call getTask for its best fits with why each one fits. In the order /tasks shows them.

One task with every listing that does it, best fit first, each with the skill that does the job when it has one. Also the slugs of related tasks and of stacks that use its listings. Use a `slug` returned by listTasks. Unknown slugs return 404.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Stable task identifier, e.g. `query-a-database`.

get.summary: Put 2 or 3 listings side by side
get.description: The comparison /compare shows, as data: for each listing, the facts that set it apart from the others ("Only one with a CLI", "No auth required", "Most skills (12)"), then one row per field with each listing's value by slug. A row where every listing agrees has `same: true`. Facts from the listings' own data, never a verdict. The same parameters as a /compare link: `a`, `b` and `c` are the columns, in order. Unknown or repeated slugs, and any past three (`d` to `f` are read so they can be named), are left out with a note in `notes`. Fewer than two listings found returns 400 with listings to put beside the one found.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: First listing's slug.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second listing's slug.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Third listing's slug.

400.description: Fewer than two of the named listings are in the directory (`error: "too_few_listings"`).

get.summary: One MCP client config for several listings
get.description: One MCP client config to paste (`{"mcpServers": …}`, as Cursor and other MCP clients read it) for up to 10 listings, and how each one connects. A listing is in the config when its own docs give a hosted server address or a local command. An MCP server whose docs give neither comes with its setup guide, and `setupPrompt` asks a coding agent to set all of those up. A listing without an MCP server comes with its CLI install command, API address or docs. Also returns a `claude mcp add` command for each server in the config, for Claude Code, and the /stack link for the listings. Nothing is guessed: every address and command is copied from the vendor's docs, as on the listing's page. The same `items` as a /stack link. Unknown or repeated slugs, listings no longer listed and any past ten are left out with a note in `notes`; none found returns 400.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Listing slugs, comma-separated, in the order to list them: 1 to 10.

400.description: None of the named listings is in the directory (`error: "no_listings"`).

get.description: A small index: the total, and the URLs of the static pages (`/catalog/{page}.json`, up to 50 listings each, featured first, then A→Z) that together hold every published agent, plus the REST search and MCP endpoints. No single request returns the whole catalog. Prefer GET /api/agents for targeted search. Built once per deploy, so it and the pages change only with a release; a deploy replaces them at the edge.

get.summary: One page of the agent catalog
get.description: Up to 50 published agents with every catalog field, including `authType` (skills are in GET /api/agents/{slug}), in the order of the index at /agents.json. `next` links the following page and is null on the last. A page past the last is a 404.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number from 1, as listed in the index's `pages`.

post.description: Speaks MCP over streamable HTTP. Exposes seven tools: `search_agents`, `get_agent`, `list_categories`, `compare_agents`, `alternatives_to`, `connect_bundle`, and `submit_listing`, which files a listing suggestion for human review. This is a JSON-RPC transport, not a REST resource. REST clients should call /api/agents, /api/compare, /api/agents/{slug}/alternatives and /api/bundle instead.

schema.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request as defined by the Model Context Protocol.

200.description: A JSON-RPC response or an SSE stream, depending on the negotiated transport.

RateLimited.description: Over 120 requests per minute from this IP. Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then retry.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the caller's window resets.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded: 120 requests per minute per IP. Retry after 42 seconds.

next.description: The same query one page on (as `offset`), or null when this page is the last.

url.description: Human listing page on Agent Switchboard.

iconUrl.description: Absolute URL of the listing's 128px PNG icon, served by Agent Switchboard; null when it has none.

accessMethods.description: How the listed product can be reached.

verified.description: Verified: we checked it works — its URLs load and its declared access (API, MCP, CLI or extension) responds. Re-checked monthly; the label drops if it stops working.

official.description: First-party listing from a major vendor (publicly traded, frontier AI lab, or ~$1B+), published under the vendor's official domain or GitHub org. Factual, not paid; separate from verified and featured.

featured.description: Featured: set only by the maintainer. With no search text, results list featured listings first, then A→Z; with search text, results are ranked by relevance and equal scores keep that featured-first order.

sponsored.description: Sponsored: a paid placement, approved by the maintainer. It shows a Sponsored label and a spot in the Sponsored slot on the homepage and the latest drop page. It never changes search results or their order, tasks, alternatives, compare or the Operator, never appears in AI-assistant (MCP) results, and is separate from Featured, Official and Verified.

officialVendor.description: Vendor behind an official listing, e.g. `Notion`; null when not official.

authType.description: How the listed product authenticates. Not used by this API.

mcpEndpoint.description: The vendor's hosted MCP server address, from its docs; null when they give none.

mcpCommand.description: The command that runs its MCP server locally, e.g. `npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest`; null when its docs give none.

quickstartUrl.description: The vendor's setup or getting-started page.

apiBaseUrl.description: Base URL of the vendor's public API.

AgentInstall.description: The command that installs its CLI, from the vendor's docs.

UseItNow.description: How to start using it, per access method, as the listing page's Use it now panel shows it. Commands and addresses come from the vendor's own docs; when there are none, docsUrl is where its instructions are. A part is null when the listing lacks that access method.

clientConfig.description: `{"mcpServers": {...}}` for Cursor and other MCP clients.

stackOfTheWeek.description: Slug of the stack of the week: the newest stack tied to a weekly drop.
